//: Type checking without a build step. VS Code reads this automatically and will
report errors inline, so no dependency is needed to benefit from it.
For a command-line or CI gate, `npm i -D typescript` and run `npx tsc -p .`;
nothing here needs to change for that, and nothing is ever emitted.
strict is off deliberately. It is the honest setting for JSDoc-annotated code
of this age -- strictNullChecks alone reports every lazily-initialised field.
The checks enabled below are the ones that catch real mistakes in this codebase:
wrong param names, misspelled properties, bad arity.
test/ is excluded on purpose. Its imports of node:test and node:assert would
need @types/node, and the tests are already verified the stronger way -- by
